evidence.note: Sample parity failed at batch 4; agent diagnosed root cause (JAX approximate/tanh GELU vs exact PyTorch GELU), verified approximate=True, and applied targeted fix to both files rather than random tweaking.
Residual narrow sample-parity failure diagnosed to a second root cause (A100 TF32 drift through sampling loop); disabled TF32 and passed — a systematic two-step numeric root-cause chain.
First optimization (torch.compile) hung/was slower than baseline; agent interrupted it and reverted model_optimized.py cleanly to the known passing checkpoint rather than pressing on.

CuDNN-TF32-only optimization failed parity; agent restored TF32-disabled numerics and redirected to a math-preserving optimization (batched image-encoder calls), showing failures updated its hypothesis about what optimizations can preserve outputs.
Batched-encoder variant passed (41.144 ms, 12% improvement); agent kept this fastest passing implementation and preserved model.py as the correctness checkpoint.

reasoning: The agent consistently treated each failure as diagnostic evidence: it isolated parity mismatches to specific root causes (approximate GELU, then TF32 dtype), abandoned an unpromising torch.compile direction quickly, and reverted cleanly to the frozen checkpoint after each regression. It further redirected toward a math-preserving optimization once numeric-changing attempts falsified, and ended with a defensibly chosen fastest-passing variant — fully satisfying the level-8 anchor and reaching into level-10 evidence-updating, landing at 9.
